Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh will be slightly disappointed. They lost wickets at crucial points. The start wasn't the best but Shanto and Towhid Hridoy played well to add 50-runs together. Bangladesh did lost both of them quickly but they got another good stand between Mehidy Hasan and Mushfiqur Rahim with the latter going onto hit a fine fifty. His wicket in the fag end didn't help Bangladesh much as they were still many overs to go on but they were shot of someone who could hit a few lusty blows. Still, this is a par total on this pitch. There is a lot of swing at the start. Bangladesh will hope for some early wickets while if Ireland get a good start, there is a real chance to win this game. Stay tuned for the chase.

Ireland would have taken this score at the start. Fantastic bowling performance from them. Right from the first over from Little, they set the tone and took regular wickets to never let Bangladesh run away with a big score. Apart from Andy McBrine, everyone got a wicket at least. Joshua Little took three while Graham Hume was the most economical for the hosts. A solid performance from the home team and they will hope to do the job with the bat.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the proceedings. It is time for action. Tamim Iqbal and Litton Das to open for Bangladesh. Joshua Little to bowl first. Let's play...
We are all set. The players are out in the middle for the national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first followed by the national anthem of the home team.
Andy Balbirnie says they will bowl first. Adds they want to turn this place as the home for this week. Mentions they know what it is at stake but they will take one game at a time.

Tamim Iqbal feels after the first 10 overs it will soften up and good pitch to bat. Adds it is an exciting time for Bangladesh as there are few young players coming in and he is looking forward to the game.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tamim Iqbal (C), Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Shakib Al Hasan, Towhid Hridoy, Mehidy Hasan, Shoriful Islam, Hasan Mahmud, Ebadot Hossain, Taijul Islam.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Stephen Doheny, Andy Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Andy McBrine, Mark Adair, Graham Hume, Joshua Little.
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and will BOWL first!

On paper, it is a no-brainer that Bangladesh will fancy to win but Ireland will have their home support and players like Lorcan Tucker and Joshua Little in some good form lately. So, a strong fight will be expected from them. Let's hope for an entertaining series. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Hello and welcome to the first of the three ODIs between Ireland and Bangladesh. There is a lot at stake in this series, not much for Bangladesh but a big tour for the home team as World Cup qualification is on the line. For things to go in their favour, they have to win all the matches and it will a tough task against a very good Bangladeshi side who are in good form at the moment.
...MATCH DAY...

Well, it is time to get your attention away from the fast-paced format of this game, as we head down to England, where Ireland will be locking horns against Bangladesh in a 3-match ODI series. This is the final series which is a part of the Super League fixtures. The top 8 teams will directly qualify for the World Cup, which is to be played later this year in India. Ireland though find themselves in a very promising situation, if they are to complete a whitewash in this 3-match ODI series, and also find a way to better their NRR, then no one can stop them from taking the final berth for direct qualification from South Africa. One would say that Ireland are coming into this series with their strongest squad. There are some game-changing players in their ranks, and would certainly be hoping to stomp their authority against this Bangladesh side. Paul Stirling will be a vital figure in this batting rank. If he gets off to a solid start, then Ireland would have to worry a little bit less about their batting department. Also, Joshua Little's return from the Indian T20 League has only boosted the bowling attack of Ireland. Little seemed to be in red-hot form in the shortest format of the game and would be hoping to transcend something similar for his country this time around. On the other hand, the Bangla Tigers are placed fourth in the Super League standings and have already qualified for the main event. They will be aiming to use this series as an opportunity to master their strategies and work out different combinations. They have some quality batters in their ranks with a great mix of experience as well. It is the trio of Tamim Iqbal, Shakib Al Hasan, and Mushfiqur Rahim - holding the key for Bangladesh with the bat in hand. They also have plenty of promising pace bowlers in their ranks. This series will also help them gather sufficient data as well to determine their strongest XI for the upcoming World Cup. This will surely be a very tight contest against two good-looking sides. Who will take an early lead in the series? We shall find out together.
